claims.statement: HJJ Theorem 1 proves almost sure recurrence for d=2 and transience for every d>=5 in the one-frog simple random walk model; Conjecture 2 leaves d=3 and d=4 conjectural.
For every real r>0, the 27-type two-step reset comparison matrix defined in exact_two_step.py for d=4, amax=3, bcap=2, ccap=2 has spectral radius greater than one.

In the HJJ deterministic one-sleeper single-entry non-backtracking model on the rooted 3-ary tree, E[V]<=3/4; the exact five-iteration rational certificate gives a slightly smaller bound. Restricted model only.

For the ordinary rooted d-ary one-frog model, d>=2, E[N_root including time zero] = d/(d-1)(1+sum_{n>=1}p_n), where p_n is the ever-activation probability of a fixed depth-n vertex. Summability gives transience; infinite expectation alone gives no recurrence conclusion.
Ordinary one-sleeper frog recurrence at original inward drift p=133/500 for every integer d>=3; hence S_3<=133/500. The unbiased T127 cases remain open.

For ordinary simple random walks on a rooted d-ary tree, killed at root returns and capped at one parent-to-subtree entry at depths 1 modulo fixed L, i.i.d. sleeping counts of finite mean mu give E[V]<=1+mu*(L*d^L/(d^L-1)-1/(d-1))<infinity. This finite-block lower model cannot prove recurrence.

The specified 27-type three-step T4 reset matrix, amax=3 and bcap=ccap=2, has spectral radius >1 at every real positive exponential weight. Exact elevated Bernstein coefficients certify all rows. No ordinary-model classification.

The stated finite activated-walk cell has exact projected first-exit PGFs from its Dirichlet/subset-closure formulas; the specified 48-type T4 cap-six mean matrix satisfies rho(M(r))>1 for every r>0. This only obstructs that comparison, with no original-model classification or established novelty.
Exploratory two-prefix-step lower frog model with three incoming types and mixed-seed star recursion; no recurrence or transience claim.

Exploratory one-retained-child-excursion lower model and two-type PGF operator; skip-tail variant at unbiased T3 drift has a positive floating-grid fixed point, not a classification of the ordinary model.

Candidate proof: self-similar and ordinary one-sleeper biased frog recurrence at original p=2649/10000 for every integer d>=3; S_3=sup_{d>=3}p_d<=2649/10000 for ordinary-model critical drifts. Unbiased T127 remains open.

An exact finite grid can establish continuous domination of T^n 1 by g_a0; a monotone physical fixed point and a Poisson improvement valid for every a>=a0 then force infinitely many returns. Full hypotheses and final-cell convex-chord condition in proof.

Candidate proof: in the ternary single-entry self-similar frog lower model at original p=331/1250=0.2648, E[V]<=49510542141875/35184372088832<141/100, hence transience almost surely. No ordinary-model transience or critical-drift lower bound claimed.
For the specified 48-type cap6 origin-and-children exit matrix on T4, rho(M(r))>1 for every r>0. This finite comparison cannot contract; no ordinary-model classification follows.
For each specified asynchronous T4 adjacent-pair map at caps (3,2) and (5,3), no positive price vector w satisfies F_(27/10)(w)<=w. Finite comparison obstruction only.

Candidate proof: the self-similar and ordinary one-sleeper biased frog models are recurrent at original p=19/80=0.2375 for every integer d>=4; S_4=sup_{d>=4}p_d<=19/80. Unbiased T127 remains unclassified.

Candidate proof: the four-child single-entry self-similar frog model at original p=2367/10000 has E[V]<=69386982371875/70368744177664<99/100 and is transient almost surely. This gives no ordinary-model transience or critical-parameter lower bound.
For the specified4260-type T4 uniform-update three-site minimum-partition map at r=27/10, no positive vector w satisfies F_r(w)<=w. Exact finite obstruction only; no ordinary-model classification.

Numerical exploration: the epsilon=1/100 fair controlled-site three-site T4 comparison at r=27/10 stays above1 at original p=0.2,0.19 and0.18. No ordinary transient interval or critical bound is established.
